Impact: wrong slugs that run words together, and two different inputs can produce the same slug. `.encode("ascii", "ignore")` deletes every character that doesn't decompose to ASCII. Before this change the regex turned those characters into separators. Confirmed outputs (base 8ffd986 -> head b0a2753): `Paris–London` (en dash) `paris-london` -> `parislondon`; `foo—bar` (em dash) `foo-bar` -> `foobar`; `Tokyo東京Osaka` `tokyo-osaka` -> `tokyoosaka`; `foo\ufffdbar` (a bad byte from fix 1) `foo-bar` -> `foobar`; `Straße` `stra-e` -> `strae`. The same deletion is why fix 1's "bad bytes become separators" clause isn't met. Suggested fix: after NFKD, drop only the combining marks, `"".join(c for c in text if not unicodedata.combining(c))`, and let the existing regex turn whatever non-ASCII is left into separators. "Café" still becomes "cafe". Add regression tests `slugify("Paris–London") == "paris-london"` and a CLI case `b"foo\xffbar\n"` -> `foo-bar`.
